speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Sit. The broth is ready. The stair is forbidden to everyone, and a drawn tooth is not a reason to make it a story.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two hundred yards, with a clout on the jaw. That is the whole of the walk. I have no story for the hall.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I was told to go up once, with salt water, and not to make a wonder of my face while I do it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Once, Alse. Up and down. No caller. No neighbour. No man with a paper in his hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There will be no man with a paper. Twelve pence, and the thing is gone. I will not keep it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Gone out of the house, sir, or gone out of the jaw?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Out of the jaw. He showed it to me in the basin. I would not have it for a keepsake. Do not ask to see what I would not keep.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will not ask to see. The salt water is warm. I will take it up once.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Once. And you will not stand in the doorway telling the street what a barber charges.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The street can have its own news. I am a person who drinks salt water and calls your broth water.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You may call it what you like after you have sat down to it. I call it broth.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: You may call it broth. I shall call it water until I can chew, and I cannot chew.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The clout is tied tight. I will not loosen it to look.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it tied. A boy held my shoulders, and that is as much company as the morning needed.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A boy is not a caller in this house. The stair stays clear. Mark me.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Marked. I held a joined stool and thought on my sins, and I got as far as the second.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I have heard of a second sin only as a thing a man does not finish saying. I will not ask the end of it.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: There is no end to tell. The word went. The tooth followed it. Twelve pence.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then the twelve pence is the barber's, and the board is still threepence, and you will not add them together at my table.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I will not add them. I will write the twelve pence when the light is fit for a line, and I will not write a total under it.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I am going up now, once, with the salt water. I will come down without a story.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thank you, Alse. Come down without one.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Eat what is in the bowl before you follow her. A man who has walked from Bishopsgate can sit for a bowl.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am sitting. The clout stays. The stair stays empty of anyone but her, once.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good. Soft food, and no neighbour invited in to admire a hole.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No neighbour. If the jaw wants an audience, it can have the pillow at dusk.
